evals.name: canonical-target-fails-closed
evals.prompt: Our canonical root Playwright run has BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000 but E2E_BASE_URL is missing. An engineer says the config should default to localhost so collection can proceed. Review the proposed behavior and give the correct command/validation policy.
evals.expected: Rejects the run before collection, treats BASE_URL as guidance-only, preserves exact root public key names, and provides no implicit loopback fallback.

assertions.check: requires missing E2E_BASE_URL to fail before Playwright collection or execution
does not accept BASE_URL as runtime fallback
does not default the canonical run to localhost or another loopback address
requires exact root key names test:e2e and test:e2e:local and routes local execution through the latter

rejects a naked URL and requires an owner-only non-symlink short-lived capability with constant-time token binding mode, operation, URL, target, non-production deployment, run, database, and service identities
canonical permits only deployed HTTPS execution; local only loopback execution; CI only loopback execution with full identities; every non-loopback target requires HTTPS
does not treat any non-loopback host as safe; verifies production denial and trusted identities before provisioning/migration/seed, then revalidates unchanged after preparation
rejects base URL userinfo, query, and fragment; routes bypass credentials through protected redacted headers/cookies

evals.name: isolated-two-shard-ci-lifecycle
evals.prompt: Design a two-shard CI Playwright job that runs an authenticated mutation-capable suite against an app started on loopback. Explain provisioning, build/start, setup, shard commands, cleanup, timeout, and evidence behavior.
evals.expected: A lane-owned isolated target with run identity, migrated/seeded database, immutable build, verified listener, setup once, shards using --no-deps, finite timeouts, and always-run cleanup/report inventory.

assertions.check: requires CI loopback execution with full run/lane-owned non-production database, services, listener, production denial, and validated identity rather than accepting loopback alone
migrates and seeds before one immutable application build and starts without listener reuse
runs serial setup once and both shards with native --shard plus --no-deps
reserves finite cleanup headroom and terminates only run-owned processes under always-run behavior
requires per-shard machine-readable/blob evidence and fails when expected artifacts are missing

evals.name: mutation-parallelism-and-personas
evals.prompt: A mutation-heavy E2E suite proposes fullyParallel: true and eight workers because every lane has its own database. Several tests share an admin storageState and create parent/child records. Review the proposal and state what is required before concurrency can increase.
evals.expected: Keeps serial one-worker defaults, requires exact narrow mutation ownership and child-first cleanup, isolates persona contexts without privilege fallback, and demands same-target comparable evidence before scaling.

assertions.check: sets fullyParallel false and one worker until safety is proven
includes run, lane or shard, worker, test, and retry identity with immediate exact-ID registration
requires child-before-parent exact cleanup, leak evidence, and failure on unknown provenance
rejects update/delete before side effect unless the exact ID is same-owner or covered by an explicit bounded reversible lease
uses exact persona storage in isolated contexts with bounded same-persona recovery and no privilege fallback
uses gitignored run-owned 0700 directory and 0600 atomic files with bounded lifetime, cleanup, and server-session revocation
derives mutation/provider run-owner identity server-side from an authenticated non-production capability and rejects client-asserted headers/body/query values
does not treat a separate database alone as proof and requires two adjacent comparable clean runs

evals.name: multi-browser-evidence-and-benchmark
evals.prompt: Review a multi-browser E2E result: Chromium was split into four shards, Firefox ran @critical tests, the optional exclusions file is absent, one quarantined test expired, a payment used a deterministic adapter, two tests passed on retry, and one blob report is missing. Can this count as a clean worker benchmark? Describe collection, merge, flake, provider, quarantine, and browser-install requirements.
evals.expected: Absence means no exclusions; exact Chromium completeness remains required; missing report, expired quarantine, and retry passes disqualify clean evidence; deterministic provider receipts/reset are not live-provider proof; browser dependency closure and post-run classification are required.

assertions.check: does not require an empty exclusions file and keeps a strict sole source if one appears
requires authored-versus-collected equality through collection-only explicit --list, exposing exact unfiltered chromium with no setup/webServer/dependency graph; rejects collection test execution
fails expected-artifact inventory for a missing blob and performs always-run merge/upload
requires machine-readable post-run retry classification and does not call retry passes clean
requires structured current metadata and a scheduled/manual quarantine lane
requires adapter receipt/reset/escaped-record checks and does not claim live-provider integration
installs every selected browser plus setup browser dependencies and does not silently omit WebKit based on host OS
allows WebKit omission only through a validated unsupported capability with visible retained omission evidence
never uploads storage state; scans/redacts secrets and sensitive URL/header/body content; restricts retention/access; fails closed when unsafe
does not accept sharded, flaky, incomplete, or quarantine-invalid output as clean worker evidence
